purpose: Re-derive equality after the foundation reset as an explicit context-local representative constraint, with relation decomposition available only through a separately admitted theory rule and never as implicit recursive graph equality.
requiredAssertions: same exact ref succeeds under an admitted atomic equality rule
different unaliased refs fail even when their self-closed shapes are observationally the same
two refs explicitly mapped to one representative under K satisfy the local atomic constraint
changing K can change the atomic equality outcome without mutating either compared relation
conflicting local representative bindings reject replay rather than choosing one
alias chaining is not followed implicitly and does not create hidden transitivity
an equality-shaped relation stored as ordinary data performs no action by itself
relation decomposition requires an exact T membership for the selected decomposition rule
one decomposition step emits exactly two pole constraints and does not recursively evaluate them
self-closed partial forms are not silently treated as complete pairs for decomposition
a root-like distinct self-cycle does not collapse to the unique root ref
shared/cyclic relation inputs remain finite because decomposition is one step over exact refs
local equality does not materialize substitution into unrelated relations
equality/decomposition replay is bound to one explicit link occurrence, so editing T/rule/K/operands on the recorded occurrence rejects
forged T, rule, K, representative, result or decomposition evidence rejects
notDecided: whether the atomic candidate becomes the canonical foundation equality relation
whether one-step decomposition is admitted by the core interpreter theory or an optional higher theory
syntax/source form for equality after grammar reset
anonymous-hole interaction beyond the preserved occurrence-local boundary
